clue.text: A sad spirit perhaps kept flying by Orwell

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the letters of the phrase a sad spirit could be arranged some other way

explanation.surface: A gloomy ghost is somehow kept aloft by George Orwell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' tells you to rearrange A SAD SPIRIT. George Orwell wrote the novel Keep the Aspidistra Flying, so the definition is the plant he kept flying.
explanation.definitionFit: Orwell's novel title Keep the Aspidistra Flying names this potted houseplant as the thing kept aloft.

clue.text: Give short name to a grass

parts.note: Alf is the familiar short form of the name Alfred

explanation.surface: Someone is told to give a nickname to a blade of grass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Give ... to' just links the pieces: put the short name ALF next to A.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfa is another name for esparto, a tough grass from Spain and North Africa used for paper and rope.

clue.text: Not entirely proper to be so cheeky

indicators.note: not entirely says only part of the words proper to is used, a run of letters taken from inside them

explanation.surface: Someone is told that being so cheeky is not quite the done thing.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit across 'proPER To'; 'to be so' is linking padding.
explanation.definitionFit: Pert describes a forward, saucy manner, a near synonym for impudent.

clue.text: US conscription authority we hear-just a lot of squares

indicators.note: we hear says the phrase from the US conscription authority is to be taken by its sound rather than spelling

parts.note: an American draft board decides who is called up for military service

explanation.surface: An American call-up office is dismissed as nothing but a bunch of fuddy-duddies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Squares' looks like stuffy people; it is the chequered pattern. British draughts is the game Americans call checkers, played on the same board as chess.
explanation.definitionFit: The playing surface for draughts (checkers) is a grid of sixty-four alternating squares and nothing else.

clue.text: Undercover dealings so disreputable ?

parts.note: underhand business deals are commonly given this adjective, which also literally means kept out of the sun, as if under cover

explanation.surface: Secret business deals are judged to be of doubtful honesty.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means both shaded from light and of questionable honesty, as in dodgy dealings.

clue.text: Sauce of queer fellow who attacks head first

parts.note: in its old sense of odd or strange, which rum also means
one who butts, ramming with the head as a goat does

explanation.surface: A dressing is credited to some odd man who charges into people with his head.
explanation.walkthrough: Rum butter is a sweet sauce of butter, sugar and rum, served in Britain with Christmas pudding; 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: This sweetened spirit-laced butter is a classic accompaniment, like brandy butter, for festive puddings.

clue.text: King Edward in Shakespeare opens the wrong way

indicators.note: the wrong way tells you to read the archaic verb backwards

parts.note: dup is an archaic verb for open, used by Ophelia in Hamlet ('dupp'd the chamber door')

explanation.surface: A monarch called Edward appears in a Shakespeare play that starts back to front.
explanation.walkthrough: King Edward is a well-known British variety of potato, not a monarch; 'the wrong way' turns DUPS round.
explanation.definitionFit: King Edward is a classic floury potato cultivar, and a spud is an informal word for a potato.

clue.text: Long-haired survivor of space train disaster

indicators.note: a disaster wrecks things, so the letters of space train are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A long-haired person is the one who lived through a crash involving a spaceborne train.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disaster' signals rearranging SPACE TRAIN. 'Survivor' points at a cat's proverbial nine lives.
explanation.definitionFit: This fluffy breed has a famously long coat, and cats are proverbially survivors with nine lives.

clue.text: Reduced to getting feathers sifted ?

parts.note: down is the soft fine feathering of birds
graded means sorted by size or quality, as sifting does

explanation.surface: Someone is reduced to the task of sorting through feathers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to getting' merely links the definition to the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To be downgraded is to be lowered in rank or status, so it means reduced.

clue.text: Warnings to shoot early callers

parts.note: to fire a gun is to shoot
alarm clocks call you early in the morning

explanation.surface: There are warnings to shoot anyone who visits too early.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Early callers' looks like visitors at the door; they are alarm clocks. 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Bells or sirens that sound when there is a blaze are warnings of danger.

clue.text: Bird needed at bar at opening time

definitions.text: Bird needed at bar at opening time

parts.words: Bird needed at bar at opening time
parts.note: a black bird's name placed before the word bar makes a lever used for prising things open; the surface suggests a pub opening

explanation.surface: Someone's girlfriend must be at the pub when it opens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bird' is British slang for a girlfriend and 'opening time' is when pubs open, but the bird is literal and joins BAR to make a tool used to force things open.
explanation.definitionFit: A black corvid whose name added to bar gives the jemmy-like lever used for forcing doors open.

clue.text: Moving line in play intended to make one jump

definitions.text: Moving line in play intended to make one jump

parts.words: Moving line in play intended to make one jump
parts.note: a cord swung round in a children's game so that the player hops over it; the surface suggests a startling line in a drama

explanation.surface: A gripping line of dialogue in a stage play is designed to startle the audience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Line' and 'play' suggest the theatre, but the line is a cord and play is a children's game.
explanation.definitionFit: A cord turned in a loop for children's games, which the player leaps over as it passes underfoot.

clue.text: Unexpectedly a swan-song for him finally

definitions.text: Unexpectedly a swan-song for him finally

parts.words: Unexpectedly a swan-song for him finally
parts.note: in the fairy tale the despised chick grows up to be a swan; swan-song usually means a last performance

explanation.surface: A performer's last appearance comes as a surprise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swan-song' normally means a farewell performance; here the end of the story is literally the bird becoming a swan, in Hans Christian Andersen's tale.
explanation.definitionFit: Andersen's mocked cygnet turns out to be a beautiful swan, so a final swan reveal is its ending.

clue.text: Sounds like wrong scoring at Bisley-got the figure wrong

indicators.note: sounds like says the phrase about shooting is to be heard, not spelt

parts.note: Bisley is a famous shooting range in Surrey, England; a scorer there tallies misses, so misses counted

explanation.surface: A scorer at a shooting competition got the total wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: Bisley, in Surrey, is the home of British target shooting, where shots that miss are counted as misses.
explanation.definitionFit: To get a number wrong when tallying is to reckon it incorrectly.

clue.text: Grandly spend about a pound leisurely

indicators.note: about here means going round, so spend is wrapped around the pound sign

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for a pound, from Latin libra
idly means in a lazy, unhurried way

explanation.surface: Someone spends lavishly, letting each pound go at a relaxed pace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grandly' is the definition at the front; 'about' wraps spend round the pound sign, and 'leisurely' supplies the last piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something in a magnificent style is doing it grandly or magnificently.

clue.text: Doctor's visitor declares himself unwilling to wait

parts.note: a person announcing who he is says I'm, a contraction of I am
someone who visits a doctor for treatment is a patient

explanation.surface: Someone in a doctor's waiting room announces he is not prepared to hang about.
explanation.walkthrough: The visitor says 'I'm patient', which written solid means the opposite.
explanation.definitionFit: Being restless and eager for something to happen now means not willing to hang on.

clue.text: Where we may see cannon moving-be sure and ram

indicators.note: moving the letters of be sure and ram around gives a new order

explanation.surface: A gunner urges a comrade to be sure to ram home the cannon while it is moving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving' signals rearranging BE SURE plus RAM; 'and' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An opening in a castle wall or parapet through which guns fire, where cannon poke out.

clue.text: Himalayan patrol car ?

definitions.meaning: the red one is a small mammal of the Himalayan forests
British police cars were once nicknamed after this black-and-white animal for their livery

explanation.surface: A police car is spotted patrolling in the Himalayas.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a small police patrol car was called a panda car from its blue-and-white or black-and-white markings.
explanation.definitionFit: The red species lives in Himalayan forests, and British slang named police patrol cars after the animal.

clue.text: Decor fashionable we hear in church

definitions.note: a phrase standing for something heard sung or said at a church service

indicators.note: something fashioned is reshaped, so the letters of decor are made into a new word

explanation.surface: Trendy furnishings are noticed at a church service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fashionable' looks like a compliment for the decor, but read as fashion-able it asks you to reshape DECOR. 'We hear' is not a sound clue here: it belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Credo, the Nicene Creed, is the statement of belief recited or sung during Mass.

clue.text: J.M. and Jack to speak for the defence

indicators.note: to speak says the two surnames are to be said out loud and heard as one word

parts.note: J.M. Barrie wrote Peter Pan, and Jack Cade led the 1450 rebellion in England

explanation.surface: Two men named J.M. and Jack are called to give evidence for the defence.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a courtroom; the defence is a physical one. Barrie and Cade said together sound like the word.
explanation.definitionFit: A makeshift wall of carts and furniture thrown across a street serves to hold off an attack.

clue.text: Ventures such as the final removal of Don Giovanni

definitions.text: such as the final removal of Don Giovanni
definitions.meaning: in Mozart's opera Don Giovanni is dragged down to hell at the end, a taking under the earth

explanation.surface: A list of risky projects includes the opera hero's last exit.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as UNDER TAKINGS, the second sense is being taken down below, as Don Giovanni is carried off to hell.
explanation.definitionFit: Enterprises or projects one commits to, and also, read in two parts, being carried off downwards to the underworld.

clue.text: One Pole allowed entrance to our shores

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
N stands for the North Pole
let means permitted

explanation.surface: A Polish immigrant is granted entry to Britain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' looks like a Polish person; it is a magnetic pole, giving N.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrow arm of the sea reaching into the coast is a way in from the water.

clue.text: Almost a mile up—-capital!

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the letters are read from bottom to top
almost means not quite all, so the last letter of a mile is dropped

parts.note: taken as written; that its letters also run backwards across the words is a coincidence of the cut-and-reverse device, not a separate hidden word

explanation.surface: Someone climbing nearly a mile high exclaims how splendid it is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' cuts A MILE to AMIL and 'up' turns it round. 'Capital!' looks like an exclamation of delight; it is Peru's capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Lima is the seat of government of Peru, a national capital city.

clue.text: Two pages employed for the long table

definitions.meaning: a single sheet in a book carries a page on each side
an extra board slotted in to extend a dining table

explanation.surface: A pair of young servants are hired to wait at a banquet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pages' suggests boy servants and 'long table' a feast, but a sheet of a book and an extending table board share one name.
explanation.definitionFit: One sheet of a book has two sides, and the removable insert that extends a dining table shares that name.

clue.text: Bound, say, to sail with this

indicators.note: say means the word for bound is to be pronounced, giving another spelling

parts.note: tied means bound with rope

explanation.surface: A sailor is obliged to set out with the boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bound' suggests obliged or heading somewhere; it is tied up. Ships traditionally sail on the tide.
explanation.definitionFit: Ships leave harbour with the ebb of the sea's rise and fall, so it is what they sail with.

clue.text: Topping device used in Parliament

definitions.meaning: topping is slang for executing, here by beheading machine
a procedural motion in the House of Commons that cuts short debate on a bill by setting a timetable

explanation.surface: A gadget for trimming the top is installed at Westminster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Topping' means executing; in the UK Parliament the same name is given to a timetable motion that cuts off debate.
explanation.definitionFit: The French beheading machine, and the British parliamentary procedure that chops debate short.

clue.text: Periods of world revolution

parts.note: each spin of the Earth on its axis marks one such span of time; the surface suggests eras of global political uprising

explanation.surface: Historians describe eras when the whole world rose in revolt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolution' suggests political upheaval, but it is the Earth turning once on its axis.
explanation.definitionFit: Each twenty-four-hour span is one complete rotation of the Earth.

clue.text: Football position to give a learner ?

definitions.meaning: the central defender's place in the traditional half-back line
read as an instruction, the middle of the word half gives A and L, that is a plus L for learner

explanation.surface: A coach decides which spot on the football team to hand to a novice.
explanation.walkthrough: L is the learner driver's plate. Read as an instruction, 'centre half' asks for the middle of HALF, which is AL: A plus L, a learner.
explanation.definitionFit: The central defender in football's traditional formation plays in the middle of the half-back line.
